newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank says rev repo falls on low interest.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank says rev repo falls on low interest.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Friday it cut its seven-day reverse repurchase rate for the second consecutive day because of banks' low participation in the operations.
The NBS' tender drained funds from the interbank money market on Friday morning at an average 14.6 percent, down from 14.95 percent, previously.

On Thursday, the NBS said it cut the reverse repo rate to signal to the market that rates should drop. But NBS reverse repo rates have been declining since last Friday due to lower commercial bank bids.

"Regardless (of) our intention to lower rates, today's rate fully generated itself as bids were insignificant compared to the current liquidity surplus, totalling 1.27 billion crowns ($38.6 million)," Peter Andresic, head of the NBS's Open Market Operation Department, told Reuters.
But local money market dealers said banks would be more willing to participate in a draining operation for a shorter term and at a higher rate.
"The central bank could have prevented (its reverse repo) rate cut if it had offered to drain liquidity for three days," Marian Tatar with ING Bank told Reuters.
Dealers estimated the market currently has a surplus of some 6.0 billion crowns in funds shorter than seven days.

According to official NBS figures, the banking sector has a liquidity surplus before Saturday's minimum reserve deadline with banks' minimum reserve demands fulfilled at 102.96 percent as of Thursday, after 102.31 percent the previous day.

"I have the impression that the market is eyeing the central bank reverse repo rate less than it is the offer and demand on the market. Trading is largely focused on one-day funds," Vaclav Petrek, a VUB Bank dealer, said.

Dealers said a gradual decline in Slovak interbank money market rates, currently levelling out to the offer range of 16.2-17.7 on all maturities except overnights, had been driven by the government's recent steps to pressure the central bank into loosening monetary policy.
-- Tatiana Vacova, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-521-8402 ($ = 32.90 Slovak Crowns)
